newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks rise, forex effect seen muted.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks rise, forex effect seen muted.

text.p: Chilean stocks rose a few notches in light morning trade as the market continued to recover ground lost to profit-taking early in the week, brokers said.

The Central Bank's loosening of controls on foreign exchange markets late Wednesday was expected to have only a marginally positive impact on prices, because the measures mainly benefit overseas investments by Chilean companies.
"They're not very relevant to our market because they are aimed at favoring investment outside Chile. I think the effect here will be nil to slightly positive," said one broker.

Other commentators said on local media that by streamlining access to formal forex markets, the measures would benefit smaller firms that want to go abroad, potentially helping their price in the long term. Chilean overseas investments have been dominated by a dozen or so big names in the electricity and manufacturing sectors.
The blue-chip IPSA index rose 0.17 percent to 118.11 points. The all-share IGPA rose 0.1 percent to 5369.55 points.
Two major banks, Banco Edwards and Banco Bice, have shareholders meetings scheduled for Thursday.
